prompt: In an accounting proof for a doubling array, cheap appends save credit for future copying. What must be true whenever a resize occurs?

options.text: Credit may go negative if the next append will repay it
options.explanation: That would spend charges not yet collected and fail to bound the current sequence prefix.

options.text: Previously collected credit plus the current charge must cover actual work
options.explanation: Correct. The proof must never spend more than it has charged.

options.text: Every item can be charged only when it is copied
options.explanation: The method deliberately charges earlier cheap operations for future work.

options.text: The resize must happen at a randomly chosen time
options.explanation: The proof concerns all allowed sequences and needs no randomness.

workedExample: Separate the immediate write from saved credits. The saved amount must already be sufficient when copying is required. If the balance becomes negative, the proposed charges or invariant have failed; expecting later operations does not repair a bound for a sequence that ends now.
